newsitem.title: USA: MassPort gives Boston zoning control on some land.
newsitem.headline: MassPort gives Boston zoning control on some land.

text.p: Massachusetts Port Authority agreed to give Boston planning and zoning approval over Massport-owned land in South Boston, the Boston Globe reported Monday.
Officials from MassPort, which owns 274 acres of land in South Boston, called the deal a victory for both sides that would promote development, the Globe reported.
The agreement between MassPort and the Boston Globe Redevelopment Authority should end years of feuding between the two agencies, the Globe reported.

Mayor Thomas M. Menino predicted the accord would push along his top economic priority -- a proposed $700 million convention center slated to be built off Summer Street in South Boston, the Globe reported.
The pact is significant because South Boston is expected to be the site of billions of dollars in new construction over the next few decades.

If the convention center wins approval, city and private developers expect a flood of tourist-related proposals, from hotels and restaurants to new retail and office space, the Globe reprorted. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
